name: Zuojiang Huashan Rock Art Cultural Landscape
description: On limestone cliffs above the Ming River in Guangxi, southern China, about 1,900 red painted figures sprawl across a rock face roughly 170 metres wide and 40 metres high. Made 1,800 to 2,500 years ago by the Luoyue people, the images show dancing humans, animals, swords and bronze drums. The paintings sit high above the water, and the surrounding karst hills and river make the setting dramatic.
